items.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: I had a chance to audition for Ozzie Nelson... I wrote an arrangement for him... I wrote a thing for him called “Rasputin’s Laundry.”... I did Ricky’s first record with Ozzie in the booth.

ctx.x: I see. He was even in that movie, “Pete Kelly’s Blues.” Do you remember that? But getting back, you were a pretty self directed young man then.

Yeah I did pretty well what I wanted to do, and I mean getting back to 1941, I don’t really remember how it happened, but I had a chance to audition for Ozzie Nelson. And I went up and played and he liked the way I played, and the thing I think that made me stay with the band, you know I wrote an arrangement for him. And Ozzie had always had one of those Dick Jurgens type bands, I mean the people danced and it was a nice dance band and he had a style where the baritone player was always roving around on the bass…
